cluster_thesis.text: The 800G-to-1.6T transition is bottlenecked on a physical input -- InP/EML light sources -- modelled 30-40% short of demand through 2029, and NVDA has committed $2bn each to Lumentum and Coherent to relieve it. A transition whose constraint is capacity rather than demand is early regardless of how far the equities have run. Co-packaged optics, usually read as the cluster's threat, is only a threat to the pluggable module layer; it raises external-laser demand.
cluster_thesis.falsifier: Two consecutive quarters of module-maker gross-margin compression while revenue still grows, or a credible supply study showing EML demand/supply crossing into balance before end-2027.

margin_pool.moving_toward: InP/EML light-source supply and vertically integrated laser capacity (LITE, COHR), plus scale-up silicon content (ALAB retiming/switching, MRVL electro-optic DSP)
margin_pool.moving_away_from: pluggable optical module assembly and copper connector / cable assembly (APH, CIEN systems integration, and the assembly half of any module maker)

evidence.claim: McKinsey projects EML supply for 1.6T transceivers falling 30-40% short of demand through 2029 -- when the scarce input is the laser, assembly becomes a pass-through and cannot hold price
evidence.source: McKinsey via semiconductor-today / tech-insider optics coverage

evidence.claim: NVIDIA committed $2bn to each of Lumentum and Coherent with purchase, capacity and R&D arrangements -- capital flowing to the laser node, not the module node
Coherent expects to double internal InP output by end of CY2026, a quarter ahead of plan, and more than double again through 2027
Lumentum's 800mW super-high-power laser is built for CPO and silicon-photonics light sourcing -- CPO removes the pluggable module's assembly value while increasing demand for this external source

reorder_when: By the ~early-Nov-2026 FQ1 prints: if COHR ships or announces qualified 1.6T volume BEFORE LITE converts its EML DR4 demo into a shipping product, COHR takes rank 1 -- the entire LITE-over-COHR call is the qualified-today-vs-promised axis and nothing else.
If LITE's Q1 FY27 actual operating margin comes in below 39% on revenue at or above the >$1.25B guide, the pricing-power premise is broken and LITE drops below COHR and MRVL.

If ALAB's Q3 2026 actual lands inside the $540-560M guide and the stock still fails to close the -6.36pp intra-cluster gap within 10 sessions, the market is pricing socket-displacement rather than mispricing growth, and ALAB moves to rank 6 or below.
If any hyperscaler names an in-house NIC or switch ASIC for volume deployment before end-2026, AVGO drops to rank 7 and APH is no longer the laggard.
If BofA's XPV off-balance-sheet exposure at AVGO is escalated at any date, AVGO becomes the laggard immediately and P-241/P-242 gains a fundamental rationale it currently lacks.
If a credible supply study before end-2027 shows EML/InP demand-supply crossing into balance, the entire margin-pool call inverts.
If CIEN delivers a second and third consecutive raise, the systems-layer-loses premise is falsified and CIEN moves above APH and GLW.

redundant_pairs.same_bet_because: Not correlation -- no return series is cached and none is asserted. On business grounds these are one position: both are InP/EML light-source suppliers levered to the same 30-40% shortfall, both build 1.6T pluggables, both supply CPO light sources, and both received a $2bn NVIDIA strategic investment in the same programme. Same constraint, same product, same anchor customer, same catalyst calendar. Together they are 4.76% of equity expressed twice.

Superficially identical -- custom AI ASICs plus networking silicon sold to the same three hyperscalers -- but they sit on OPPOSITE sides of the same share shift: the Google/Marvell share story the book files as evidence_against AVGO is precisely MRVL's bull case. Holding both is a hedge on which way that socket moves, not a doubled exposure.

CRDO's active electrical cables are the technology that REPLACES passive copper as the reach budget collapses at 1.6T -- long the same rack as APH while short APH's specific structural failure mode.

Below $180, or on any hyperscaler in-house-switch headline that de-rates it without touching its share. Caveat consistent with my own margin-pool call: ANET is on the assembly/systems side of the migration, so this is a substitution within a losing layer.

thesis_tensions.tension: AVGO is the only `watch` name in this cluster yet ranks mid-ladder, above four `strengthening` names. On the playbook's own axes AVGO is one of the two strongest positions here, and its Q3 print -- +86% revenue, AI semis +221% YoY -- is not a `watch` print. The `watch` status is carried by the XPV financing overhang and the light Q4 guide, which are capital-structure and expectations facts, not competitive-position facts. This ladder is NOT endorsing the sell leg of P-241/P-242 on cluster grounds.

Ranked laggard while state.thesis carries it as `strengthening`. The thesis is `unverified` with an evidence_against array that explicitly records no check was performed, so the label rests on segment classification rather than evidence. My rank rests on the connector/copper stack position being the layer the margin pool is leaving. Neither side is strongly evidenced -- resolve by an actual APH earnings and news check.

CIEN was upgraded on 2026-09-03 for a clean beat-and-raise and I still rank it 6th of 7. I am not disputing the print; a transport/systems assembler buys the constrained input that LITE and COHR sell, so the same tailwind reaches CIEN's P&L with worse economics.
No tension in direction -- but the ladder ranks ALAB three places ABOVE its price standing. The deciding fact is the ~30% guide-over-consensus gap dated 2026-08-05, not the month of price.
